title: Three-Color Dango
text: “Whatever happened at the arena, sounds like you cheated your way through it, but the world ain’t that easy! I’ll show you the harsh reality of it, the true meaning of strength, indeeeeed!”

Takt drew out his claws with all the leisure in the world and swung them at Wolf. Hmm, I could deflect it, but stray shots wouldn’t come my way regardless, so I supposed I’d act to capture him alive too. First, I needed to instantly kill Takt’s Dragon Emperor to make approaching easier, I say. Next up was the pig in the red hood, wearing an especially unpleasant scowl as she oinked.
“GRAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!”
Takt, wearing a fearless grin as Wolf stepped forward to lunge at him, fired off that one skill he apparently only knew, using his claws.
“This one suits you perfectly, don’t it? Die! Vanzin Claw!”
“Wolf!”
Father leapt in to shield Wolf and hold him back. It happened in an instant, so even Crocodile Guy and the others were too slow to react.
“Hey, wait!?”
“Iwatani-sama!?”
“Wha—!? Father!?”
Clang! Takt’s skill grazed Father’s shoulder, sending sparks flying. Given Father’s defense, even a direct hit wouldn’t amount to much damage these days.
“Yipe!? GRAAA—!?”

Wolf, restrained in an unexpected hold, was about to howl in fury, but upon realizing his captor was Father—and simultaneously feeling the attack land on Father’s shoulder, drawing a bit of blood—his pupils began dilating and contracting, and he started trembling. Something like a trauma trigger seemed to be flashing through his mind.
“Wolf, you okay? Seems like you’ve got some history with these guys, but if you lose yourself like that and lunge in, it’s gonna be a problem, so calm down.”
Father gently scolded him, blood trickling slightly from his shoulder, and Wolf just opened and closed his mouth repeatedly like a fish. His hand trembled as he touched the blood on his shoulder.
“What, tryin’ for sympathy points? Nobody cares about some cowardly little runt’s sob story!”

Takt raised his claws again, ready to press the attack on Father and Wolf mid-exchange. Don’t get cocky, I say! Just as I rushed in to swing my spear, Wolf—snapping back to his senses at the attack—hoisted Father up and… leapt in a great bound toward me.
“I won’t… let you. Not anymore… I won’t lose… to fear. I won’t run.”
Wolf forced the words out.
“Wolf? You can talk—”

And then Wolf, as if entrusting the matter, handed Father off to Crocodile Guy and the others. Wasn’t I standing right here? If he’d entrusted Father to me, I’d have protected him no matter what happened, I say! I felt I’d need to have a word with Wolf later about why he hadn’t handed Father to me instead. As if to say “it’s fine,” Wolf turned his back—reason apparently restored—and gave Father a thumbs-up.
“AWOOOOOOOOOOOOO!”
Then he let out an even bigger roar. Magic power and ki gathered around Wolf, and his body grew a size larger. Looked something like a transformation.
“Huh? The hell are you so pleased about just dodging a bit. You’re still just some trembling little mutt like always.”
“Oink oink oink oink!”

With a click, the red-hood pig, leading the charge among the pigs, whipped out firearms and let loose a volley at Wolf. Oh, that again. Well then, timed with that volley, I’d go ahead and blow a hole through Takt’s Dragon Emperor’s forehead, I say.
“Gyaa—”
But Takt, too absorbed in the volley, didn’t notice.
“Haaah!”
Wolf dodged every single bullet raining down and arrived right in front of Takt. He drew back his claws even wider.
“Better than I expected, but eat this! I’m gonna finish you off properly! With the very claws you love so much!”
Takt seemed to be going for some kind of finishing move, slashing at Wolf with his claws, but Wolf’s abilities now outclassed his.
“Gau!”
Slash! The arm bearing Takt’s claw went flying.
“Ohhh—!? Ha! Blew his arm clean off… didn’t I?”

Seeing the severed limb fly, Takt apparently thought at first it was Wolf’s arm that had been blown off. But he tilted his head, noticing Wolf’s claws were still firmly attached, and then looked down at his own arm. A moment later, blood sprayed out.
“GYAAAAAAAA!? My arm—my arm!?”
“Oink!?”
“Oink oink oink!”
“Takt’s hand—!?”

Too noisy, I say! I hurled a Second Javelin at Takt’s Griffin and finished it off. I’d already blown the head off Takt’s Dragon Emperor with an Air Strike Javelin, mind you. Fresh blood sprayed in three directions at once.
“—AAAAAAAAA!?”
Well, Takt clearly didn’t understand the situation in the slightest—he only seemed shocked that one of his own arms had been blown off.
“I won’t stop anymore. I’ll avenge my brother’s regrets!”
Just then, the severed claw lying on the ground, glimmering, shone brightly and settled into Wolf’s hand.
“That claw is… but no… surely, no matter how you look at it, that’s strange, isn’t it?”
Rabbit Guy seemed to have sharp eyes and noticed the claw.
“This is my brother’s claw… I see, so you were held down by that man too, and it left you resentful, didn’t it.”
Wolf seemed to be speaking to the claw as if addressing it directly.
“Y-you bastard! What the hell are you doing!? Give it back! That’s mine, dammit! Just ’cause you blew off my arm, don’t think I’m gonna kill you nice and easy!”

Takt, apparently finally coming back to his senses, shouted with rage boiling over. What remained was that troublesome fox. I turned it into a Beast Lance and blew its head off with an auto-triggered Air Strike Javelin. Since most of the pigs had their attention fixed on Takt’s injury, they barely noticed my attacks. In my head, Father from the first world was groaning, exasperated, “How many are you picking off in the middle of all this chaos,” but it’s their own fault for not noticing, I say. Wolf, unlike before, now seemed to be settling into a proper stance to fight. “Reason restored” would be the accurate way to put it.
“Oink oink! Oinkeeeee!”
Just then, whether trying to create an opening for Takt to attack or simply displeased that Wolf was shining, the red-hood pig approached and hurled a hand grenade.
“Hmph.”
Wolf batted the grenade away before it could explode. The blast echoed through the back alley.
“Oink oink oink oink!”
Wolf glared at the red-hood pig with eyes filled with quiet fury.
“You’re a vile, rotten woman, you… disgustingly ugly, and unsightly.”
“Oink!? Oink oink oink oinkeeee!”
The red-hood pig seemed to be hurling insults at Wolf while flipping him off.
“You thieving bastard!”
“You’re the thief here. I’ll make you spit out exactly how a Whip Hero managed to steal my brother’s claw. But before that… take this. HAAAAAAH!”
The claw seemed to glow and awaken with light as Wolf spoke, but tormenting Takt was my job, so I’d have to interrupt, if you please. Without further ado, I hit Takt with a Paralyze Lance X.
“Unfortunately, that’s as far as you go, I say.”
“Wha—”
Wolf’s claw sliced cleanly through empty air.
“Guah! Wha—y-you—!? Guh!? GUH!!!?”
I drove my spear straight through, and while I was at it, swung around and skewered the red-hood pig along with him.
“P-pig-kun! Oi—”

Just then, Takt’s creepy, love-sick maid pig came running up, so I skewered her too as a bonus. I’d turned Takt, the red-hood pig, and the maid pig into a lovely three-color dango. Fuahahaha! What a filthy little skewer, I say. As for the rest, I might as well pull out another spear and wipe them all out. Before capturing Takt, I made sure to lock onto every single pig I’d properly identified in the surrounding area.
“Aiming Lancer X, I say!”
With a whoosh, I hurled it and blew every last one of their heads clean off.
